verdict: Netflix turned 12% revenue growth into 37% profit growth — its operating margin hit 34.6%, and the streaming machine now funds record share buybacks.

segments.name: Streaming
segments.note: Memberships and advertising — effectively all of Netflix's money comes from people watching series, films and live events. Ads are still a small slice (about $2.7B expected for all of 2026) and are not reported separately.

opex.name: Sales & marketing
opex.note: Advertising the service and winning members.

opex.name: Technology & development
opex.note: Building the app, the recommendation engine and the streaming technology — Netflix's version of R&D.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Running the company day to day.

takeaways.title: Margins keep climbing
takeaways.text: Operating margin rose from 28.2% to 34.6% in a year; Netflix guides to 31.5% for 2026 as a whole, even after a Q4 charge for job cuts.

takeaways.title: Ads: growing, but slower than hoped
takeaways.text: Netflix cut its 2026 ad-revenue expectation to about $2.7B from roughly $3B — the ad business is real money now, but still only about 5% of revenue.

takeaways.title: Record buybacks
takeaways.text: Netflix repurchased $4.8B of its own stock in one quarter — its biggest buyback ever — with $22.3B of capacity still unused.

otherDetail: Interest expense of $185M on Netflix's $15.3B of debt, partly offset by $43M of interest and other income — a net $142M cost below operating profit.
follow100Note: The rows reconcile to $100 within a cent of rounding.
footerNote: Per-share figures reflect Netflix's 10-for-1 stock split of November 14, 2025. Netflix reports a single operating segment, so the flow starts from total streaming revenue.
